title: QCQS line section algebra, coproduct comparison and affine evaluation charts
statement: Let $f:X\to T$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], and let $L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Put $\mathcal A=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}f_*L^{\otimes n}$, with $L^{\otimes0}=\mathcal O_X$, direct image $f_*N(V)=N(f^{-1}V)$ and tensor-product multiplication [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] [def-weil-pbc-graded-sheaf-structures]. Then $\mathcal A$ is a quasi-coherent graded $\mathcal O_T$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-algebra]. The canonical comparison $c:\bigoplus_{n\geq0}f_*L^{\otimes n}\to f_*(\bigoplus_{n\geq0}L^{\otimes n})$, whose restriction to the $n$th summand is the direct image of its coproduct inclusion, is an isomorphism of graded algebras. Let $P=\operatorname{Proj}_T(\mathcal A)$ [def-nagata-relative-proj] and let $\psi:f^*\mathcal A\to\bigoplus_{n\geq0}L^{\otimes n}$ be evaluation, using module pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]. There is the canonical $T$-morphism $r:U(\psi)\to P$ of [lem-trf-space-line-module-proj-map]. For every affine open $V\subseteq T$, put $W=f^{-1}V$ and $M=L|_W$. There are canonical identifications $\mathcal A(V)=\Gamma_*(W,M)$ [def-sc-invertible-section-ring] and $P\times_TV=\operatorname{Proj}(\Gamma_*(W,M))$ [def-pc-proj]. Under these identifications, the induced graded map $\mathcal A(V)\to\Gamma_*(W,M)$ is the identity, $U(\psi)\cap W=\bigcup_{n\geq1,\ s\in\Gamma(W,M^{\otimes n})}W_s$, and $r|_{U(\psi)\cap W}$ is the usual canonical map for that identity graded map, where $W_s$ is the nonvanishing open of [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. These identifications respect further affine restriction, multiplication and the unit. In particular, if these nonvanishing opens cover every such $W$, then $U(\psi)=X$.

source.place: Tag 01VJ (lemma-characterize-relatively-ample), (3) implies (5), section algebra and adjunction map; Schemes Tag 01LC (lemma-push-forward-quasi-coherent); Constructions Tag 01O9 (lemma-invertible-map-into-relative-proj), clause (3).

proof.text: Put $N_n=L^{\otimes n}$ and $B=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}N_n$. On an affine open with a frame $e$ of $L$, the frame $e^{\otimes n}$ identifies $N_n$ with $\mathcal O$, also for $n=0$. Thus every $N_n$ is quasi-coherent by the affine-local definition [def-sc-invertible-module, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, pqf-def-coherent]. The homogeneous multiplication sends $(a e^{\otimes i},b e^{\otimes j})$ to $ab e^{\otimes(i+j)}$; replacing $e$ by $ue$ multiplies both sides by $u^{i+j}$, so these formulas agree on overlaps. Associativity, commutativity and the unit are the corresponding identities for local coefficients.

source.place: Tag 01VJ (lemma-characterize-relatively-ample), (3) implies (5), tensor-power algebra; elementary local-frame verification.

proof.text: Apply [pqf-lem-pushforward-qcoh] to each $N_n$: its morphism hypothesis is exactly the assumed quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of $f$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-coproduct-closure] on $T$ to these direct images, and on $X$ to the $N_n$. This proves quasi-coherence of $\mathcal A$ and $B$. For an open $V\subseteq T$, multiply $s\in(f_*N_i)(V)$ and $t\in(f_*N_j)(V)$ by their tensor product on $f^{-1}V$. The structural unit sends $a\in\mathcal O_T(V)$ to $f^\sharp(a)\in(f_*N_0)(V)$. The preceding identities and restriction of sections give precisely the homogeneous operations of [def-weil-pbc-graded-sheaf-structures], hence a graded algebra whose underlying module is quasi-coherent [def-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-algebra].

source.place: Tag 01LC (lemma-push-forward-quasi-coherent); Tag 01ID (lemma-colimit-quasi-coherent) and Section 01LA, arbitrary sums; applied as in Morphisms Tag 01VJ.

proof.text: Fix $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq T$, $W=f^{-1}V$ and $M=L|_W$. Restriction to an open preserves coproducts [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits]. For $E_n=(f_*N_n)|_V$, the counit isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] identifies $E_n$ with $\widetilde{E_n(V)}$; its colimit assertion and unit isomorphism therefore identify $\Gamma(V,\bigoplus_n E_n)$ with $\bigoplus_n E_n(V)$, by the map from the inclusions. By the definition of direct image, $E_n(V)=\Gamma(W,M^{\otimes n})$. Consequently $\mathcal A(V)=\Gamma_*(W,M)$ [def-sc-invertible-section-ring], canonically and degree by degree. The multiplication and unit on both sides are the tensor product of the same sections and the section $1$, so this is an identification of graded rings.

The affine $V$ is qcqs [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Base change and composition in [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], parts (3) and (2), imply that $W\to V$ is qcqs and that $W$ is a qcqs scheme. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits], $B|_W$ is the coproduct of the $M^{\otimes n}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-cohomology-direct-sum] with $p=0$ on $W$. Here $H^0(W,F)=\Gamma(W,F)$: in the resolution definition [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology], degree zero is $\ker(\Gamma I^0\to\Gamma I^1)=\Gamma(\ker(I^0\to I^1))=\Gamma F$, since sections of a kernel are exactly sections killed by its map. Thus $\bigoplus_n\Gamma(W,M^{\otimes n})\to\Gamma(W,B|_W)$ is bijective. Under step 3 this is precisely $c(V)$, since on summand $n$ it is $\Gamma(W,N_n\to B)$. Hence $c$ is an isomorphism: these maps are bijective on every affine open, a basis, and their inverses commute with restrictions by uniqueness. On homogeneous local sections, $c(st)=c(s)c(t)$ and $c(1)=1$, by the inclusion multiplication in $B$; by local finite sums the equations hold on the whole coproduct. Therefore $c$ is an isomorphism of graded algebras.

source.place: Tag 01FF (lemma-quasi-separated-cohomology-colimit), degree-zero direct-sum specialization; also Modules Tag 01AI (lemma-section-direct-sum-quasi-compact). Scheme hypotheses: Tags 01K5 and 01KU.

proof.text: Take the mate of $c:\mathcal A\to f_*B$ under [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction], giving $\psi:f^*\mathcal A\to B$. In the tensor definition [def-pc-module-pullback], its degree-$n$ formula is $a\otimes s\mapsto a\,s|_O$ on a source open $O\subseteq f^{-1}V$, for $s\in\Gamma(f^{-1}V,N_n)$. The tensor balancing relation is exactly $f^\sharp(r)a\otimes s=a\otimes rs$, and both sides evaluate to $f^\sharp(r)a s$. Thus this is evaluation; it preserves the multiplication and unit just constructed. In particular, the induced map $\mathcal A(V)_n\to\Gamma(W,M^{\otimes n})$ sends $s$ to $s$, so its graded ring map is the identity under step 3. For $V'\subseteq V$, both ways of applying evaluation to $s$ give $s|_{f^{-1}V'}$; products restrict as $(st)|=s|\,t|$ and the unit restricts to $1$.

source.place: Tag 0096 (lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules), explicit tensor/restriction adjunction; applied to the map in Morphisms Tag 01VJ.

proof.text: By [lemma-nagata-relative-proj-exists], $P$ exists and $P\times_TV=\operatorname{Proj}(\mathcal A(V))=\operatorname{Proj}(\Gamma_*(W,M))$, with chart identifications commuting with further affine restriction. The scheme clause of [lem-trf-space-line-module-proj-map] gives the canonical $T$-morphism $r:U(\psi)\to P$. To compute its domain over this fixed $V$, [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections] says that on each affine $O\subseteq W$, $f^*\mathcal A_n$ has sections $\mathcal A_n(V)\otimes_R\mathcal O_X(O)$, generated by the pulled-back $s\in\mathcal A_n(V)$. Their evaluations are precisely the sections $s$ in step 5. After choosing a frame of $N_n$ at $x\in W$, $\psi_n$ is surjective at $x$ exactly when these coefficients generate the unit ideal of the local ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}$. If they do, a finite combination equals $1$, so at least one coefficient is a unit; conversely a unit coefficient generates. By [def-sc-section-generating-locus], this says $x\in W_s$ for some $s\in\Gamma(W,M^{\otimes n})$. Taking $n>0$ proves $U(\psi)\cap W=\bigcup_{n>0,s}W_s$.

source.place: Tag 01O9 (lemma-invertible-map-into-relative-proj), opening definition of U(psi) and clause (3); Tags 01NQ (lemma-glue-relative-proj) and 01I9 (lemma-widetilde-pullback), affine local descriptions.

proof.text: On $W_s$, with $s$ of positive degree $d$, [lem-trf-line-proj-affine-chart-atlas] characterizes the canonical map into $D_+(s)$ by $b/s^k\mapsto\psi(b)/\psi(s)^k$ for $b$ of degree $kd$. Step 5 turns this into $b/s^k\mapsto b/s^k$, where on the right the ratio is the coefficient of $b$ relative to the invertible section $s^k$ of $M^{\otimes kd}$. This is exactly the chart formula for the usual canonical map associated with the identity of $\Gamma_*(W,M)$. The chart theorem's uniqueness and overlap compatibility identify the two maps on all of $U(\psi)\cap W$. Its compatibility with affine refinements, together with the restriction-compatible charts of [lemma-nagata-relative-proj-exists], gives the asserted further affine restriction: the fraction $b/s^k$ is sent to $b|/(s|)^k$, which is the restriction of its coefficient. Multiplication and the unit were checked in steps 3 and 5. Finally, if every such $W$ is covered by its $W_s$, step 6 gives $W\subseteq U(\psi)$; the inverse images of affine opens cover $X$, so $U(\psi)=X$.

tool_uses.why: Generic qcqs direct-image quasi-coherence theorem (01LC), required for each graded piece; the unit has no alternative direct-image theorem.
Generic closure under arbitrary sums, needed for the underlying section algebra; the unit has no closure theorem.
Generic affine module equivalence and colimit preservation, used to compute sections of the algebra coproduct.
Generic canonical direct-sum theorem, specialized to H^0 on each affine preimage; no cohomological route is substituted for a unit step.
Generic module adjunction, constructing evaluation as the mate of the coproduct comparison.
Generic relative-Proj existence and restriction charts, needed for the codomain and its affine identification.
Generic affine tensor formula, used to check the fixed-affine generation locus.
